gaps.sentence: The doctor has ___ detailed records of every patient since 1990.
gaps.explanation: keep records (of something) is the fixed collocation for storing information.

gaps.sentence: The company has ___ enormous losses this quarter.
gaps.explanation: 'Suffer losses' is the standard collocation for experiencing financial loss.

gaps.sentence: Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.

gaps.sentence: Smoking can ___ serious harm to your health.
gaps.explanation: do harm to something is the fixed phrase; 'make harm' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: I must ___ my homework before I can go out.
gaps.explanation: do homework is the fixed collocation; 'make homework' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ great fun at the fair.
